cues.text: Sunlight looks white, but it is a mix of every colour.
Each colour is a wave. Red light has long waves, blue light has short ones.
The air is made of tiny molecules of nitrogen and oxygen, far smaller than one light wave.
When a wave passes a molecule, it makes the molecule's electrons shake, and the molecule throws a little of that light off in every direction.
Short blue waves shake it much harder: blue is thrown off about five times more than red.
So most of the red goes straight on, while the blue gets spread around the sky.
Now you, standing here, looking up at this patch of sky, away from the Sun.
No sunlight comes straight at you from there. What reaches your eye is only the light the air threw sideways, and that is mostly blue.
Every molecule in the air does the same, so wherever you look, blue light comes at you from all over the sky.
That is the blue of the sky: sunlight, sorted by the air.
